observed.behavior: Calls module.eval and torch.onnx.export with do_constant_folding=True; chooses dynamo=False where supported.
Tracing selects _slow_forward, which invokes self.forward in Python.
The exporter transforms params_dict through eval peephole and constant folding.
Lifted parameters become registered buffers in an export wrapper; any changed version causes re-export and native program reimport.
Lowered weight uploads include native casts/transposes; imported program does not retain a full original-Torch-weight to folded-initializer dependency/update recipe.

constraints.scope: Arbitrary torch.nn.Module ingestion through the currently supported exporter
constraints.conclusion: Calling the exporter from Mojo would still execute Python forward. There is no native translation of arbitrary Python forward in this implementation. Preserving this feature requires an explicit external-capture policy decision or a new supported frontend contract; no Mojo defect is established.

Not claimed impossible or blocked by Mojo. Correct native refresh needs parameter provenance and recomputation of folded dependency values, or a native FX frontend covering the supported graphs. Blind original-weight replacement or dynamicizing every weight does not preserve all existing exported graphs and their arithmetic.
